# F1 and F2 closed, and two procedural mistakes of mine that the journal should carry

RED is record 65, 481 tests with thirteen failures, and GREEN is record 66, the same 481 passing; the full suite
is 1,413. Nine of the thirteen were `AssertionError: HarnessError not raised`, which is the gate accepting what
must be refused, and the other four were the two disclosure tests and the two pack tests.

**F1, and it was a regression the judge-by-green change introduced.** An exempted red skipped every attribution
check rather than only the tree comparison, so a slice entry could join one round's red to another round's green
even where the journal attributed that red elsewhere, and the round whose own red had passed could advance on it
while the honest citation of its own red was refused for not having failed. `_the_journal_puts_it_elsewhere` now
owns the contradiction question in both directions, a number the chain contradicts and a null where the chain
named a slice, and the exemption block asks it. The reviewer's reproduction is refused by name.

What a red is now held to, written into `cited_check`'s docstring rather than left implied: a non-zero exit that
`checks.demonstrates_failure` holds of; its phase and its stage; its place in the order; the route of the position
its entry declares; the attempt of its green; and the journal's attribution wherever an accepted tdd record has
made one. What is not checked, also written down: the tree it ran against, which is the exemption, and the
pairing inside a single attempt, because an accepted record can only attribute a check recorded before it, so
there is nothing to attribute the checks a record cites in its own attempt. The earlier disclosure claimed nothing
distinguished one slice's red from another's, which was false, and the "Nothing else." paragraph that carried it is
gone.

**F2 is closed with a floor rather than an equality, and the argument is the interesting part.** A null round is
held to the strictest route in the plan, not to none. An equality would be unsatisfiable on a plan routed to two
tiers, and the way out of an unsatisfiable rule is to name a position the round does not have, which is the lie
the gate exists to make unnecessary. A route guards against work done under a weaker model than the plan judged
necessary; a stronger one is a cost, and a round belonging to no single slice has no routed cost of its own. Same
reasoning as the union: it touched several, so it answers to what all of them ask. The implementer explicitly did
not conclude "nothing, because shadow is on", on the ground that a rule written only when it starts biting is a
rule written under pressure.

Measured for both: 277 citations and 101 pairs across every journal, none cross-attempt, none split across
attempts, and **no red an accepted record puts elsewhere**, so F1 moves no recorded verdict. Sixteen entries
declare null; with shadow true none is refused, and counterfactually with shadow false fourteen of the sixteen
would be, all fourteen on the context half and none on the model floor, so no recorded null round ran below its
plan's strictest tier. The parity the finding asked about holds: with shadow off the numbered rule already refuses
ten of the thirteen numbered entries, so the truth was never the cheaper declaration.

A fifth file was necessary and is disclosed rather than hidden: `harness/tests/test_routing.py` contained a test
asserting the hole itself, a null round declaring haiku against a money-rule opus slice, accepted, with a
docstring saying it was held to no route. It is flipped to the refusal with the way through added.

**Two mistakes of mine, recorded because the journal should carry them.** The fourth review's `return` was never
written, so the ticket sat at review while a fix round tried to record tdd checks, which the stage correctly
refuses; that is why records 65 and 66 were reproduced from a saved patch rather than recorded as they were made,
and why record 64 is a rejected RED that exited 0 against a tree that already held the fix. And the commit whose
message describes that return also carries the fix's production half, because a `git add -A` swept it in: the
message and the diff disagree, and this record says so rather than leaving a reader to find it.
